It is proposed that formal land use planning and zoning regulations shall mandatorily incorporate critical parameters such as the availability of trunk infrastructure, including water supply, electricity, and sanitation systems, to ensure that development is aligned with service capabilities. and hazard-based restrictions.

construction areas

awareness and implementation.

3.Establishing a regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on availability of trunk infrastructure

There is a need to establishing a regulatory framework that defines zoning parameters based on the availability and adequacy of trunk infrastructure. This framework shall ensure that development permissions are granted only where infrastructure systems are sufficient or planned to meet the projected demand, thereby preventing overburdening of services and ensuring orderly growth.

4. The above proposed measures are expected to result in a scientifically robust and legally enforceable planning system that promotes sustainable development, enhances public safety, protects natural resources, and ensures efficient utilization of infrastructure. It will also improve transparency, strengthen governance, and support informed decision-making.

The White Paper on fiscal management of Tamil Nadu that was published in June 2026 sets the roadmap for better revenue mobilisation and administrative reforms, and has inter alia observed that the decline across major taxes like GST, VAT, and excise including revenues from mines and minerals has been mainly driven by administrative choices, leakages and corruption in the past rather than an underlying economic slowdown. Some of the key factors highlighted in the White Paper are outlined below:

e Own-tax effort at a historic low — the SOTR-to-GSDP ratio fell to 5.45% in 2025-26, the lowest in two decades showing the sharpest decline among peer States in recent years.

e Unique to Tamil Nadu — Peer States like Maharashtra, and Karnataka have held on or have shown growth in SoTR-GSDP ratio, while Tamil Nadu alone has registered a steady decline.

e Broad-based weakness — the fall is reflected in all major taxes: GST, VAT on petroleum, State Excise, Stamp Duty and Motor Vehicle Tax.

e Cause is administrative, not structural — attributed to leakages, systemic corruption and administrative choices, primarily in commercial taxes, registration, excise and mining.

6.2. Protection of Traditional Fishing Rights

of Tamil Nadu Fishermen

The Palk Bay region, comprising the

districts of Nagapattinam, Tiruvarur, Thanjavur

Pudukkottai, Ramanathapuram and supports

32

10,559 motorised fishing crafts and 550 non-

motorised fishing crafts, with a fisherfolk

population of about 2.09 lakh living in

286 fishing villages. Nearly 80,000 fishermen

directly depend on fishing for their livelihood.

Protecting the traditional fishing rights and

livelihood of Tamil Nadu fishermen, particularly

those operating in the Palk Bay, continues to be

one of the foremost priorities of the

Government. Fishing communities in the Palk

Bay region have traditionally depended on these

waters for their livelihood. However, frequent

apprehension of fishermen and seizure of fishing

boats by the Sri Lankan Navy on allegations of

crossing the International Maritime Boundary

Line (IMBL) have caused considerable hardship

and insecurity among the fishing community.

The Government has, therefore, consistently

pursued legal, diplomatic and administrative

measures to safeguard the interests of

33

Tamil Nadu fishermen and secure a permanent

solution to this persistent issue.

6.2.1 Efforts to Safeguard Traditional

Fishing Rights through Retrieval of

Katchatheevu

The Government of Tamil Nadu has

consistently maintained that the restoration of

the traditional fishing rights of Tamil Nadu

fishermen in the Palk Bay requires the retrieval

of Katchatheevu, which was ceded to

Sri Lanka in 1974.

6.2.2 Efforts for the Release of

Apprehended Fishermen and Fishing Boats

The Government has been consistently

pursuing the release of Tamil Nadu fishermen

and their fishing boats with the Government of

India. The Hon'ble Chief Minister has repeatedly

taken up the matter with the Ministry of External

Affairs and the Hon'ble Prime Minister, besides

34

raising the issue during the 11th Governing

Council Meeting of NITI Aayog held on

11.06.2026, seeking urgent intervention for

securing the release of apprehended fishermen

and fishing boats.

Between 01.01.2021 to 28.08.2026,

1,691 Tamil Nadu fishermen were apprehended

by the Sri Lankan Navy. Of these,

1,653 fishermen have been released and

repatriated. Continuous efforts are being made

to secure the release of the remaining

38 fishermen and 269 fishing boats presently

under the custody of the Sri Lankan

Government.

6.2 SERVICE UNITS OF TCMPF

6.2.1 Aavin Frozen Semen Production Station, Nilgiris

This was established in 1973 to produce

high-quality frozen semen straws for artificial

insemination (AI), thereby supporting genetic

improvement and productivity enhancement of

dairy animals.

The station produces frozen semen straws

from Jersey, crossbred Jersey, Holstein Friesian

and crossbred Holstein Friesian breeding bulls.

The frozen semen is subsequently stored and

distributed through the Semen Distribution Centre

60

at Erode to the DCMPUs for use in artificial

insemination programmes.

At present, this station maintains 99

breeding bulls, of which 64 bulls are under semen

collection. The farm follows stringent Government

of India biosecurity protocols to ensure the

maintenance of disease-free breeding stock and

the production of high-quality frozen semen.

During 2025–26, the station produced 16.85 lakh

frozen semen doses. The farm is ISO

9001:2015 certified and has been awarded

“A” Grade Certification by the Central

Monitoring Unit, Government of India,

reflecting its adherence to the highest

standards of quality and biosecurity.

6.2.2 Frozen Semen Distribution

frozen semen doses produced.

lakh cattle frozen semen doses and 0.14 lakh

buffalo frozen semen doses were distributed.

Mission – Progeny Testing Programme (RGM-PTP)

are reared at the Quarantine Station, Erode

before being inducted into frozen semen

production stations across the country.

2.7.7 Flood Mitigation Works

Urban coastal areas are more prone to

flooding than rural coastal areas due to their high

population density, extensive built-up

infrastructure and reduced natural drainage. The

concentration of critical infrastructure and

economic activities in urban areas increases the

potential for damage and disruption during flood

events. In contrast, rural coastal areas generally

have lower population densities and larger natural

open spaces that help absorb and store excess

rainwater, thereby reducing flood impacts. Hence

it is necessary to manage the urban floods with

proper drainage system.

Major flood-prone areas are Chennai,

Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, Cuddalore,

7.4.3 Restoration of degraded coastal wetlands focusing on seagrass meadows in Gulf of Mannar, Tamil Nadu

Seagrasses are highly productive coastal

wetlands that provide habitat for fisheries, marine

reptiles and mammals, while acting as powerful

35 times faster than tropical rainforests. Under

the Tamil Nadu Wetlands Mission, in collaboration

meadows in the Gulf of Mannar near Koswari

Island was restored.

The work for preparation of brief documents

Tamil Nadu, has been initiated.

7.5 Tamil Nadu Coastal Restoration Mission

The TN-SHORE project promotes coastal

resilience and sustainable marine resource use

through a multi-sectoral approach, integrating

ecological, socio-economic and infrastructural

goals. It supports a circular blue economy,

local livelihoods and capacity building.

This component of the TN-SHORE project aims

to strengthen institutional capacity for the

comprehensive conservation of coastal and

54

component include:

• Biodiversity Conservation Park at

Kadambur, Chengalpattu District.

• Sea Turtle Conservation Centres at

Chennai and Nagapattinam.

• International Dugong Conservation

Centre at Manora, Thanjavur District.

• International Bird Centre at

Marakkanam, Villupuram District.

• Conservation and Restoration of

Coastal Wetlands.

These centres and programs are designed to

support species protection, habitat restoration,

research, awareness generation and community

engagement along Tamil Nadu’s coastline.

55

This TN-SHORE project component focuses

on coastal protection using an Ecosystem-based

Approach (EbA) and green infrastructure

(living shorelines) emphasizing mangrove and

seagrass restoration.

This approach enhances ecosystem services

and supports carbon credit trading

for climate-resilient, sustainable coastal

management.

livelihoods by promoting sustainable opportunities
